summary.headline: Saksoft Q2 FY27 revenue flat QoQ at about INR249 crores; PAT up 10% QoQ to INR32 crores on a 12.92% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR249 crores, broadly flat QoQ, while EBITDA fell 4% QoQ to about INR44 crores with margin down 66 bps to 17.6%. PAT rose 10% QoQ to about INR32 crores. H1 FY27 operating income was INR497 crores (down 2% YoY), with EBITDA down 8% YoY to INR89 crores. Management attributed flat revenue to AI-driven efficiency cannibalisation, client insourcing and slow US pipeline conversion, and said H2 will be better than H1 without quantifying it.

segments.commentary: 16 clients above USD1 million annual revenue; top 5 about 40%, top 10 about 58%, top 20 about 72% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management says H2 FY27 will be better than H1 and improve quarter by quarter; it did not quantify this beyond the 'around INR1,100 crores' figure cited for H2 in one answer.

FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,200 crores (cited by analyst; another analyst cited INR1,250 crores) was not firmly reiterated; management said it depends on 'non-linear options' such as M&A and partner-led pull and called it a tough ask.
Long-term ambition of USD500 million revenue by 2030 described as a 'mammoth' target; management said it is confident of getting close to it, if not reaching it.
EBITDA margin can return to 19-20% over the next 2-3 years, but not in the next two quarters due to sales and leadership investment and the shift to outcome-based pricing.
Employee cost may weigh on margins for one or two quarters because of senior hires, then stabilise as revenue rises.
Management said the only metric to watch is top-line growth.
capex_capacity: No capex plan or capacity utilisation figures were disclosed; utilisation (excl. trainees) was 84%.
Management plans to raise sales cost (about 3% of total cost today) in a phased manner as quarters improve, mainly in the US.
Plans to increase presence in APAC GCCs (mainly India and Singapore) and in the UK, Europe and US; no new geography planned.
M&A funded from internal cash, with limited debt and no equity dilution; management cites over 8 acquisitions in the last 10 years.
demand_pricing: US pipeline is not converting at the pace expected, while UK and Europe conversions were good; management blamed internal follow-through rigour, not a loss of pipeline.
AI-led efficiency gains (cited as 30-50% in product engineering and 20-30% in managed services) are cutting client revenue in the short term; price increases only partly offset this.
Some clients are insourcing work to captive centres, which management called temporary blips.
Traction is strongest in engineering and in managed operations (infrastructure and application support), which carry 2-5 year contracts.
Competition from Tier 1 and Tier 2 IT firms moving into mid-size deals; management says it sees no impact from vendor consolidation.
Outcome-based revenue is rising, but no current share was disclosed (analyst cited about 10% last year).

qa_highlights.question: How will the USD500 million revenue target by 2030 be funded and split between organic and inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the target mammoth but said it is confident of getting close to it, if not reaching it. It is pursuing M&A, partner-led pull (ServiceNow, Salesforce) and campaigns. M&A will be funded from internal cash and limited debt, with no equity dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,200 crore FY27 guidance still valid, implying about 40% growth in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on non-linear options that could significantly lift revenue, called it a tough ask, and said investments come before results. Another analyst cited INR1,250 crores; management said a number close enough is possible if options work.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook if nothing non-linear materialises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be better than H1 and suggested around INR1,100 crores. It said Q3 was about half complete with good visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the retail weakness and the loss in some accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no client was lost, but some projects with existing customers ended, and this should pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins return to 19-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the next two quarters, given sales and leadership investment and the shift to outcome-based work. Management said it is definitely possible within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI deflation being offset by pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no rate cuts, only revenue cuts from efficiency. Price increases offset only part of the loss, so short-term revenue falls before clients return with more work.

risks_watch: Revenue cannibalisation from AI-led efficiency, with the company smaller than Tier 1 and Tier 2 peers that can offset it across large contracts.
US pipeline conversion, and whether the new CEO (joined about 3 weeks before the call) and US sales changes lift bookings.
Client insourcing to captive centres, which management called temporary.
Margin pressure from senior hires and sales investment for one to two quarters.
Whether the INR1,200 crore FY27 revenue target and the USD500 million 2030 ambition are met, given that M&A and partner pull were not quantified.
Outcome-based revenue share; management gave no number.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term direction and H2 recovery, but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers. Management gave no quantified pipeline or outcome-based revenue share and deferred several answers to follow-up. It acknowledged internal execution gaps in US conversion.
key_quotes: We have to demonstrate much more growth than we have in the last 4 quarters, which have been predominantly flat.
Second half will definitely be better than the first half. That's not saying much because first half has been flat.
Pipeline in the U.S. has not been materializing at the pace at which we would have liked or expected.
We need to have more rigor. And with Gurmeet joining and physically being present there in the New York region, it will help.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of INR1,200 crore was held but management called it a tough ask dependent on non-linear options (M&A, partner pull), with a fallback of about INR1,100 crore; H2 improvement was not quantified and the US pipeline is not converting, so growth is weakly backed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell 66 bps QoQ to 17.6% and H1 margin is 17.93% (down 107 bps YoY); management said 19-20% will not come in the next two quarters due to sales and leadership investment and outcome-based pricing shift, with 19-20% only in 2-3 years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new capacity, plant or facility was announced; utilisation is 84% but the call discussed only sales-cost build-up and APAC GCC presence expansion, not physical capacity additions.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 operating income fell 2% YoY to INR497 crores and Q2 was flat QoQ at about INR249 crores; H2 is guided better than H1 (around INR1,100 crores fallback) but US pipeline conversion is weak and AI cannibalisation and insourcing are cutting client volumes.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 84% (above the 80% threshold) with no capex plan disclosed, though M&A funded from internal cash (net cash INR244 crores) is the more likely route to added capacity than organic capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 INR1,200 crore target was only held as a tough ask dependent on non-linear options; the fallback is about INR1,100 crores, which implies H2 revenue well above H1 (INR497 crores) and H1 is down 2% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue is INR497 crores, so INR1,200 crores needs about INR703 crores in H2 (about 40% above H1), and management's own fallback is INR1,100 crores, which needs about INR603 crores in H2; the US pipeline is not converting and AI deflation is cutting client revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management pursues partner-led pull (ServiceNow, Salesforce) and outcome-based offerings, but no specific product or model launch was named or dated.

rows.label: APAC GCC and UK/Europe/US presence expansion
rows.why: Management plans to increase presence in APAC GCCs (India and Singapore) and UK, Europe and US, with UK and Europe conversions described as good, though no new geography is planned and no quantified target was given.

rows.label: M&A funded from internal cash
rows.why: Management cites over 8 acquisitions in 10 years and says M&A will be funded from net cash of INR244 crores with no equity dilution, but no specific deal was named and the non-linear options are unquantified.

rows.label: US share of revenue to at least 55%
rows.why: US is 51% of H1 FY27 revenue and management wants at least 55% in the near term, but US pipeline conversion is currently lagging, so the shift depends on the new CEO and US sales changes.
